headline: One follow-up needs doing before the next release.
lede: The first review found eight small gaps. The session proposes doing one now, four later, and skipping three. Change any call you disagree with.

rows.action: Teach the sample tool’s report to read the new config format.
rows.why: Configs now save as TOML; until this lands the report shows nothing for a new config, and the next release depends on it.
rows.detail: From sample#36: `src/report.js` `configPathFor` reads only `<name>.json`, so it can't show a `.toml`. Your ruling, 2026-10-12: land before the next release.

rows.action: Make the checker catch a note written after a title or heading.
rows.why: A note there silently cuts the title short, with the link built from it. Not seen in a real config yet.
rows.detail: From sample#1: `title` and `heading` are not prose fields, so `title: X # note` is cut at the comment with no finding.

rows.action: Flag a link that points only at “#”.
rows.why: It passes silently today, and it’s rare.
rows.detail: From sample#1: a bare `#` link target passes silently.

rows.action: Check that each config’s path points inside the repo.
rows.why: A path outside the repo sends the link warnings to the wrong place.
rows.detail: From sample#1: `config.path` is not validated as repo-relative.

rows.action: Replace a needless pattern match with a plain text search.
rows.why: Tidier code, no change in behavior.
rows.detail: From sample#1: `bracketRe` is a regexp for a literal `[`.

rows.action: Skip the empty-list warning when a list is empty.
rows.why: Harmless as it is; an empty list is rare.
rows.detail: From sample#1: a `sentence` with `items: []` still gets the warning.

rows.action: Read the data folder once per run, not once per config.
rows.why: Only a speed-up, and runs have few configs.
rows.detail: From sample#1: `loadData` re-reads the data directory for each config.

rows.action: Move the end-to-end test’s program path out of a shared variable.
rows.why: It’s the standard Go test setup; nothing to gain.
rows.detail: From sample#1: `e2e` keeps the built binary path in a package global.
